verdict.rationale: First-party docs say Memories let ChatGPT carry useful context from earlier chats into future work (docs-63, docs-19). Codex CLI's /memories command controls whether a chat uses existing memories or feeds future ones (docs-35, docs-80), and Projects add shared context across related chats (docs-15). The community remark about 'limited memory' (comm-3) concerns instruction drift within a single session, not cross-chat memory, so it does not create a dispute. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that memories are actually applied in new chats, and documented memory review/management controls in the main ChatGPT app (only CLI controls are shown).
